2020_147_031720bdmtg.paragraph: Packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of March 17, 2020, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It carries the agenda, minutes of the February 11, February 18 and February 25, 2020 meetings, the January 2020 Treasurer's Report with its complete check register plus PCard and wire-transfer listings, and three business items covering furniture, audit services and paging upgrades. The consent-agenda budget amendment sets the 2019-20 General Fund appropriation at $162,228,130, with an ending fund balance of $24,123,476 projected for June 30; total district disbursements in the January period were $8,388,472.76.

Troy School District Board of Education, regular meeting agenda of March 17, 2020, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

## Consent agenda (item 5)
Minutes of the February 11, 2020 special meeting and closed session (p. 4), the February 11 workshop (p. 6), the February 18 special meeting (p. 7) and the February 25 regular meeting (p. 10); Treasurer's Report - January 2020 (p. 20); General Fund Budget Amendment (p. 104); High School Cooperative Agreement (p. 111). Business items follow: Furniture (p. 115), Audit Services (p. 120), PA System (p. 122).

## Minutes carried in the packet
February 18: Resolution 20-018 appointed Mrs. Vital Anne to the seat vacated by Mrs. Paula Fleming for a term ending December 31, 2020, on a 6-0 roll call after a nomination round in which Mrs. Emina Alic drew 1 Yes and 5 No. February 25: Resolution 20-020 named February Principal Appreciation Month (7-0); Resolution 20-022 closed Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder, Boulan Park, Athens and Troy High to open enrollment for 2020-2021 except for not more than 25 incoming ninth graders; Resolution 20-023 authorized a limited Schools of Choice program under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 30 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 13 total sixth-through-eighth grade nonresident students. Bid awards ran from the Niles Relocation Project at $1,645,048.50 to an iPad purchase from Apple Computers at $367,500.00.

## Agenda and consent items
The consent agenda (item 5) carries minutes of the February 11, 2020 special meeting and closed session (p. 4), the February 11 workshop (p. 6), the February 18 special meeting (p. 7) and the February 25 regular meeting (p. 10); the Treasurer's Report - January 2020 (p. 20); the General Fund Budget Amendment (p. 104); and the High School Cooperative Agreement (p. 111). Business items are Furniture (p. 115), Audit Services (p. 120) and PA System (p. 122).

## Minutes reproduced
February 11 special meeting: President Schmidt presiding, with Gottlieb, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present and Mrs. Hammond participating by remote communication; administrators Machesky, Birmingham, Carrier, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris and West. Tony Lucchi, Troy Education Association President, addressed the Board. Resolution 20-017 moved closed session for negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) at 5:07 p.m., reconvened 5:10 p.m., adjourned 6:10 p.m.; the closed-session minutes record a call to order at 5:12 p.m. The February 11 workshop opened at 6:17 p.m. with about 13 audience members including eight candidates for the vacant seat, heard Troy resident Russel Reynolds on Bid Pack #26 Pool Equipment, and took Business Services items plus Schools of Choice 105 and 105c and Media 2.0 updates; adjourned 9:55 p.m.

February 18 special meeting: eight candidates sought the seat vacated by Mrs. Paula Fleming for a term ending December 31, 2020. Dr. Philippart nominated Mrs. Vital Anne and Mrs. Hammond nominated Mrs. Emina Alic; the roll call on Mrs. Alic was 1 Yes, 5 No, and on Mrs. Anne 6 Yes, 0 No. Resolution 20-018 appointed Mrs. Vital Anne, 6-0. Resolution 20-019 moved a negotiations closed session at 7:14 p.m., reconvened 7:18 p.m.; adjournment 9:15 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

February 25 regular meeting: called to order 7:01 p.m. with about 115 in the audience. New trustee Vital Anne, a Troy resident of 16 years with a master's degree in mechanical engineering, was introduced. Tim Fulcher, Director of Athletics, recognized twelve Fall 2019 all-state athletes, and Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal of International Academy-East, was honored as 2020 Michigan ASTA Administrator of the Year, a nomination described by Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction. Resolution 20-020 recognized February as Principal Appreciation Month, 7-0. Resolution 20-021 approved the January 7 workshop minutes, the January 21 organizational and regular meeting minutes, and the December 2019 Treasurer's Report, 7-0. Enrollment projections by Plante Moran CRESA supported flat enrollment for budget and planning. Resolution 20-022 closed Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder, Boulan Park, Athens and Troy High to open enrollment for 2020-2021, excepting not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area wishing to attend Athens, 7-0. Resolution 20-023 accepted applications under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 30 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 13 total sixth-through-eighth grade nonresident students, limited to districts within or contiguous to the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, 7-0. Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, reported on Schools of Choice and Media 2.0.

Bid awards, all 7-0: Resolution 20-024 Niles Relocation Project, $1,645,048.50 (2016, 2019 and 2020 Capital Projects Fund); 20-025 Network Cabling - ITT Building to MOSS, $39,841.21; 20-026 Site Work Projects, $2,117,078.78; 20-027 Flooring, $934,459.00; 20-028 Bid Pack #26 Pool Equipment, $258,037.50; 20-029 Bus Purchase from Hoekstra Transportation, $732,136.00; 20-030 Audio Video Upgrade for the Services Board Room to MOSS, $63,398.45; 20-031 TCCHS Smart Board Displays to VSC, $44,525.54; 20-032 Asbestos Removal to BDS Environmental, printed as $308.700.00; and 02-033 as printed, iPads and cases from Apple Computers, $367,500.00. Student representatives reported Athens Charity Week raising $180,024.40 for Elli's House and Troy High Activist Week raising $16,000 for Whitmer School in Pontiac; TCCHS history teacher Jeff Rainwater was named TSD Teacher of the Year among 44 nominees. Governor Whitmer was to visit March 2 to shadow Wass teacher Kristyn Cubitt. Adjournment 8:52 p.m.

## Item 8.A - Furniture Purchase, Elementary
Kris Griffor led a project team with TMP Architecture (1191 West Square Lake Road, Bloomfield Hills, Michigan 48302; TMP Project No. 20003) to evaluate Elementary Media Center furniture under the Media 2.0 program. The recommendation letter of March 10, 2020 to Ms. Kristine D. Griffor was signed by Keri Seeney, NCIDQ, Interior Designer. Each elementary selected kits up to $80,000, with PTO funds covering extras, except Martell, which receives complete replacement after a flood. Award total $899,485.81 from the 2016 and/or 2019 Capital Projects Fund: Dew-El $121,223.65; Interior Environments $5,670.00; Interior Office Source $112,331.00; Great Lakes Furniture Supply $302,814.00; NBS Commercial Interiors $357,447.16. ## Item 8.B - Professional Audit Services
Memo of February 28, 2020 from Rick West to Dr. Rich Machesky and the Board: the RFP issued in January with proposals due February 12th; six proposals were received and two firms, Plante Moran and Yeo & Yeo, were interviewed on February 27th by Kandice Moynihan, Pat Orczykowski, LaTisha Goulbourne, Josie Simon, Margaret Weaver and West. The award to Plante Moran, PLLC, consistent with its proposal dated February 12, 2020, carries not-to-exceed fees of $57,500.00 for 2019-2020, $58,600.00 for 2020-2021, $59,700.00 for 2021-2022, $60,900.00 for 2022-2023 and $62,100.00 for 2023-2024, from the General Fund; the June 30, 2019 annual audit cost $57,750.

## Item 8.C - Paging Upgrades
RFP #9899 was issued January 27, 2020 for district-wide paging upgrades; sealed bids were opened February 18, 2020 with two compliant proposals, The DataCom Group at $778,105.00 and Moss at $1,114,132.00. Eric Helsel, RCDD/OSP/RTPM, Project Manager, Convergent Technology Partners of Swartz Creek, recommended the low bidder in a February 27, 2020 letter to Technology Director Beth Soggs after a February 25th interview; DataCom previously installed paging at the ECC and IAE. The award is $855,915.00, the base bid plus an approximately 10% contingency of $77,810.00, from the 2016 and/or 2019 Capital Projects Fund.
